title: Embryos in large groups form a 'hyperembryo' that resists teratogens better

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Embryos in large groups form a 'hyperembryo' that resists teratogens better

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Individual embryos raised in large groups form a kind of 'hyperembryo' with its own distinct transcriptome and an ability to resist teratogenic challenges far better than individual embryos or small groups.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Applications and a Roadmap Toward a Radical Regenerative Medicine › Top‐Down Control Exploits Agential Materials by Pushing Complexity from the Engineer onto the System Itself

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For example, the hypothesis of scale‐free biology [196] has led to the discovery that individual embryos in large groups form a kind of “hyperembryo” with its own unique transcriptome and an ability to solve teratogenic challenges far better than individual embryos (or small groups) exhibit [197].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Applications and a Roadmap Toward a Radical Regenerative Medicine › Top‐Down Control Exploits Agential Materials by Pushing Complexity from the Engineer onto the System Itself”. Scope: Groups of Xenopus laevis embryos (author's lab's prior work, ref [197])

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-19: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Protection and transcriptomic difference are clear measurable outcomes and may be represented in public sequencing repositories. Existing studies can test the reported Xenopus phenomenon, but environmental confounds and the collective-entity interpretation limit discrimination.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare malformation and survival under identical teratogen doses across isolated embryos, small groups and large groups, and test for a group-specific transcriptomic state. A size-dependent protection effect plus reproducible differential expression supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Raw group-level phenotype data may not be deposited.

Hyperembryo is an interpretation, not a separate measured entity.

Group density changes chemistry and dose exposure as well as communication.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.7
data adequacy: 0.5
data existence: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: GSE245782 is an open test of the transcriptome clause: large versus small groups, treated and untreated, at two stages, can be reanalyzed with ordinary differential-expression methods. The claim also says large groups resist teratogens far better than individuals or small groups, and that morphological outcome is not in the sequence archive. Expression can be resolved now; the resistance half cannot.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reanalyze RNA-seq from large versus small Xenopus cohorts, with and without teratogen, and test for a cohort-size-specific expression signature. Separately, morphological protection would be scored as the rate of teratogen-induced defects in large versus small groups. A distinct large-group transcriptome and a lower defect rate would support the claim; no expression difference and no survival advantage would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A modest gene list may be a group-size effect without establishing a hyperembryo that resists teratogens far better.

The deposit is one species and one teratogen, thioridazine.

Defect and survival rates are not in the expression matrix.

data existence: 0.72
analysis feasibility: 0.75
